column2: A jaggery mountain with ten loads is the best, the next two by halves; a gold Meru with a thousand palas is the best, likewise the next two.
A sesame mountain with ten drona, five and three in order; a cotton mountain with twenty loads, ten and five;
a ghee mountain with twenty pots of ghee is the best; a silver mountain with ten thousand palas is the best;
a sugar mountain with eight loads; the middle and lowest by halves each. I shall tell the ten cows, giving which one shares enjoyment and liberation.
The first is the jaggery cow, and another the ghee cow; the third the sesame cow; the fourth the water cow;
the milk cow, the honey cow, the sugar cow, the curd cow, the juice cow, and the tenth is the cow by form; the rule is stated.
For the liquid cows there are pots; for the others, heaps. A black antelope skin four cubits long, neck to the east, should be placed on the ground,
smeared with cow-dung, with darbha spread all around; a small antelope skin likewise should be prepared for the calf.
One should arrange the cow facing east, with feet to the north, with her calf. The best jaggery cow is always of four loads;
the calf should be made of one load; of two loads the middle is remembered; the calf of half a load; the lowest of one load;
the calf of a quarter, according to the jaggery wealth. Five krishnalas make a masha; sixteen of those a suvarna;
a pala is four suvarnas; a tula is remembered as a hundred palas; a bhara is twenty tulas; a drona is four adhakas.
Both the cow and calf of jaggery, covered with white fine cloth, with ears of shell, feet of sugarcane, eyes of pure pearl,
with veins of white thread, with white blankets, backs of copper pots, with white chowries as hair,
with brows of coral, with udders of butter, tails of silk, milk-vessels of bronze, pupils of sapphire,
with horns and ornaments of gold, hooves of silver, teeth made of various fruits, noses made of scent —
having made them, one should worship the cow with these mantras, best of twice-born: "The Lakshmi of all beings, who abides among the gods,
may that goddess in cow form give me peace. She who dwells in the body, Rudrani, ever dear to Shankara,
may that goddess in cow form remove my sin. The Lakshmi on Vishnu's breast, the Svaha of the fire,
the power of moon, sun and stars — may she in cow form be for my prosperity. The Lakshmi of the four-faced, and the Lakshmi of the lord of wealth,
the Lakshmi of the world-guardians — may that cow be boon-giving to me. You are Svadha of the chief ancestors, Svaha of the sacrifice-eaters;
the cow removes all sin; therefore grant me peace." The cow thus invoked one should offer to a Brahmin.
The rule for all cows is the same. Having obtained the fruit of all sacrifices, he is stainless and shares enjoyment and liberation.
A well-behaved cow with golden horns, silver hooves, joined with cloth, with a bronze milk-vessel, a milk-giving cow with fee should be given.
The giver of her attains heaven for years equal to the hairs; if a tawny cow, she saves again up to the seventh generation.
Having given a cow with golden horns, silver hooves, bronze milk-vessel, with fee according to ability, one shares enjoyment and liberation.
Having given a cow with two heads (in the act of calving), for as many ages as the hairs of the calf, one gains heaven; one should give by the earlier rule.
By one near death a cow with calf should be given as before. At the gate of Yama, great and terrible, is the hot river Vaitarani;
To cross it I give this black cow, the Vaitarani cow.
Having made a silver wheel, one should have it given while holding it on the head, joined with gold, to a Brahmin: this is the great Wheel of Time.
One who gives iron equal to oneself does not go to hell. One who offers an iron staff of fifty palas,
covered with cloth, to a Brahmin has no Yama's staff. Roots and fruits and the like, or substance, together or singly,
with an intention of conquering death, one should give for increase of life. A man of black sesame should be made, with silver teeth and golden eyes,
with raised sword in hand, tall, with a disc of hibiscus color, wearing red garments, garlanded, adorned with a conch-garland,
feet with pair of sandals, with a black blanket at the side, holding a lump of flesh at the left: the Time-Person.
Having worshipped him with scents and the like, one should present him to a Brahmin; he is free of death and disease and becomes lord of kings.
Having given a cow and bull to a Brahmin one obtains enjoyment and liberation. Having given a golden horse under Revanta one is not subject to death.
Even a single one filled with bells and the like, having given, one shares enjoyment and liberation. One who gives gold obtains all desires.
When gold is given, silver is the fee; for other gifts too gold is remembered as the fee.
Gold, silver, copper, rice and grain, daily ancestral rite, worship of gods — all this lacks a fee.
Silver as fee for the father is the accomplisher of dharma, desire and wealth. Gold, silver, copper, gems, pearls and riches —
all this the great-minded gives who gives the earth. Ancestors who dwell in the ancestor-world and gods in the gods' place
are satisfied by the peaceful-souled one who gives the earth: a market-town, a village or a grain-rich village,
or a hundred nivartanas, or half that, or a house and the like — even a cow-hide measure of land given, he shares in all.
As a drop of oil spreads in water, so the gift on earth spreads; the fruit of all other gifts follows one birth;
of gold, land and cows, the fruit follows seven births. Having lifted twenty-one families, the giver of a maiden shares the Brahma world.
Having given an elephant with fee one becomes stainless and shares heaven. Having given a horse one obtains life, health, good fortune and heaven.
Having given a maidservant to a best of Brahmins one reaches the world of Apsaras. Having given a copper dish of five hundred palas,
or half, or half of that, one obtains enjoyment and liberation. Having given a cart with oxen, one shares heaven with a vehicle.
By giving clothes one obtains life, health, and imperishable heaven; the giver of grains, wheat, rice, barley and the like shares heaven.
Seat, metal vessel, salt, scent and sandal, incense, lamp and betel, iron, silver and jewels,
divine various substances — having given, one shares enjoyment and liberation; having given sesame and a sesame vessel one obtains heaven.
There is nothing greater than the gift of food, nor was nor will be; gifts of elephants, horses and chariots, maids, servants and houses
do not deserve a sixteenth part of food-gift. Even having done very great sin, whoever afterward becomes a giver of food
is freed from all sins and obtains imperishable worlds. Having given drinking water and a water-shed one obtains enjoyment and liberation.
Having given fire and wood on the road and the like, one obtains radiance and the rest; he is attended in heaven in an aerial car by gods' and Gandharvas' women.
Having given ghee, oil and salt one obtains everything; having given umbrella, sandals, wood and the like one lives happily in heaven.
On pratipada and chief tithis, in yogas like Vishkambha, at the beginning of Chaitra, of the year, at Ashvini and the rest,
having worshipped Hari, Hara, Brahma and world-guardians, the gift is of great fruit. Planting groves of trees, feeding and the like, road-service and the like,
foot-anointing and the like — having given, one obtains enjoyment and liberation. Three are of equal fruit here: cows, earth and Sarasvati (learning).
Having given Brahmi Sarasvati, one becomes stainless and shares Brahma's world. He who gives knowledge of Brahman is the giver of the earth of seven continents;
a man who gives fearlessness to all beings shares in all. A Purana, the Mahabharata or the Ramayana,
having written and given the book, one obtains enjoyment and liberation. He who teaches Veda, scripture, dance and song shares heaven.
One should give wealth to the teacher and food and the like to the students; what remains ungiven by that seer of dharma, desire and the rest?
The fruit of a thousand Vajapeyas well performed — all that fruit is obtained by the gift of knowledge, without doubt.
In a Shiva temple, Vishnu's house or the Sun's temple, he who reads a book aloud would be a giver of all gifts.
In the three worlds the four castes, the four stages separately, and all deities from Brahma are established in the gift of knowledge.
Knowledge is the wish-granting cow; knowledge is the supreme eye; by giving Upavedas he rejoices with Gandharvas;
by gift of Vedangas one obtains heaven; by gift of dharma-shastra he rejoices with dharma;
by gift of siddhantas he surely obtains liberation; by giving a book he obtains the gift of knowledge.
Having given scriptures and Puranas one obtains everything; one who teaches disciples obtains the fruit of the lotus;
having given that by which he lives, there is no end to the fruit. What is best in the world and also dear to oneself,
all that should be given to ancestors by one desiring imperishability for them. Vishnu, Rudra, the lotus-born, the Goddess, Vighneshvara and the like,
one who worships and gives substance for worship shares in all. One who has a temple and image made obtains everything;
the one who sweeps and smears becomes stainless; in the work of many mandalas, he becomes the lord of a mandala.
